checks.tolerance: Hides source object key 622 (folder), exports the original scene and reimports it: the folder reads back hidden and the character inside it stays visible. The CharaStudio side of ST-T03 visibility (reloading the exported scene in the original player) is not covered here.

Renames source object key 622 (folder), exports the original scene and reimports it: the new name reads back. Camera and route renames are not exercised because the fixture scene contains neither object type; the character-name rejection half of ST-T03 rename is a StudioModel export guard covered by the Engine suite.

Edits face slot 20 on character key 0 and body slot 0 on character key 65, exports the original scene and reimports it: both rates read back within 1e-5. The inspector's live visual update and Reset to card are not covered (no headless pixel or reset assertion).

Edits the body.skinMainColor card color on character key 0, exports the original scene and reimports it: the edited rgba reads back on every component within 1e-5. The hair color edit is NOT part of this scenario: hair.parts.0.baseColor is a draft color on this card but binds no material on the imported assembly, so export skips the writeback; the live preview update and Reset to card stay unchecked.

With IKKOKU_STUDIO_ITEM_CATALOG set, the import diagnostics must report `Items rendered from the converted catalog: 19; unmapped keys: none.`, and an export of all 19 placeholder items plus a reimport must still report that line. The rendered transforms and saved colors of the props (the visual half of ST-T04) are not asserted.

On scene-x (two active cameras, IKKOKU-A key 0 and IKKOKU-B key 2) the import must pick the last active camera in depth-first order (key 2) as the load winner; toggling camera 0 must make it active, and after export+reimport the written flags must make key 0 the winner again. This exercises our own load/export rule (ST-A06/ST-T03 active camera); reloading the exported scene in the original CharaStudio player is not covered.

On scene-x, toggling the active camera key 2 off must leave no active camera (orbit view); export writes every camera flag false and a reimport must still show no active camera. Deactivating key 0 (not the winner) is not scripted; the reload happens in our importer, not the original player.

Renames camera object key 0 on scene-x, exports the original scene and reimports it: the new name reads back on the camera placeholder (the camera-object half of ST-T03 rename, which the folder-only rename-folder scenario could not reach). The active-camera flags stay untouched by the rename; the winner (key 2) is not re-asserted here.

On the stt11c route scene (routes key 0 and key 3, both saved active) the inspector must report key 0 playing; toggling it must stop it, and after export+reimport key 0 must read back stopped (its flag written) while key 3 still reads back playing (its flag untouched). Only the play-state flag round trip is asserted; whether the character actually animates along the route is not observable headlessly.

On scene-x the two camera objects and the scene light must be live at load; renaming the folder placeholder (key 1) and undoing must keep the look-through winner (key 2), both camera entries and the scene light (before ST-T15 the undo emptied all of them), and redoing must re-apply the name. Toggling to camera key 0, exporting and reimporting must read back key 0 active: the export only rewrites the active flags because the load-winner record survived the undo. ST-T15/ST-T01 camera half.

The props scene's 19 converted item assets and the scene light must be live at load; hiding folder key 622 and undoing must restore it visible with all 19 item entries and the scene light still cached (before ST-T15 the undo emptied them), and redoing must hide it again. Export+reimport re-asserts the hidden folder and the 19-item diagnostic. ST-T15/ST-T01 props half; the rendered assets themselves are only censused, not pixel-checked.

On the stt11c route scene, stopping route key 0 and renaming key 3 then undoing must keep both route runtimes live (2 entries; before ST-T15 the undo dropped them), roll the key 3 name back, and keep the runtime play state: key 0 stays stopped because play state is runtime-only and never part of an undo snapshot. Export+reimport then reads key 0 back stopped (its flag written by the export) and key 3 playing. ST-T15/ST-T01 route half; whether the character animates along the route is not observable headlessly.
